_about: One entry per seat: identity, the state files it reads and writes, and its switches. dt.py and delvetown_monitor.py both read this file, so they cannot disagree about a seat. Data only: there is one code path for every seat. install-monitor.sh copies it to ~/.local/state/delvetown-dt/seats.json, where both programs look first. File names are relative to that directory; an environment variable (DT_PUBLISH_LOG, DT_SESSION_CACHE, ...) still overrides any of them.

akai.name: akai
akai._sig_why: The name jev gave on 2026-10-11 (bid 3mxm4wmrm7j2f), adopted 14:47:33Z for one week; the end is a moment, not a date (leaflet 3mxmpb47nmz2f).

quietyear._why: The Quiet Year repo work: a burst of town messages only the Quiet Year session can answer, because only it works in the repo. scripts/lane_relay.py wakes that session with what arrived, once a burst has settled, and never more often than every 50 minutes (min_gap_s 3000): steady traffic still arrives as one burst per interval, and a lone item waits at most one interval. It acts on its own; the operator is not in this loop.

locksmith._env_file_why: akai's .env holds akai's app password: this seat names its own with DELVETOWN_ENV_FILE, or reads none.
locksmith._files_why: The names in use on 2026-10-24, kept as they are so nothing moves on disk. The key-versus-handle mix is history: dt.py named some files for the key, the monitor named all of them for the handle.
